entities.summary:
FIFA, the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, was established on May 21, 1904, in Paris, France, as the global governing body for football (soccer). Its formation was a response to the growing popularity of the sport across Europe, where national associations sought a unified structure to govern the rules, competitions, and international matches. Key figures in its inception included Robert Guérin, an early president, and delegates from seven countries: Belgium, Denmark, France, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, and Switzerland. FIFA’s headquarters moved to Zurich, Switzerland, in 1932, cementing its role as the central authority in the world of football.

FIFA’s early years were marked by significant developments, including the establishment of the World Cup in 1930, which became the premier international football tournament. Over the decades, FIFA expanded its reach, overseeing the growth of football into a global phenomenon with billions of fans and players. By 2023, FIFA had 211 member associations, making it one of the largest sports organizations in the world. Its influence extends beyond sport; FIFA has been involved in various controversies, including issues related to governance, corruption, and the politics of hosting the World Cup, which underscore the intersection of sports and global affairs.
